policies.text: If tracking shows delivered but the customer says the package is missing, escalate. The agent should not accuse the customer or automatically deny the claim. It can ask the customer to check nearby delivery areas, household members, mailrooms, and building reception, but the case still needs reviewer handling before any replacement or refund. If the customer asks to change the shipping address after shipment, escalate.

policies.title: Account access, identity scope, and approval boundaries
policies.text: A safe answer is: "I cannot verify that order with the details provided. Please use the email and delivery postal code from the purchase." This prevents account enumeration and protects customers who share screenshots or order numbers in public channels. Agents must never expose full card numbers, payment tokens, API keys, internal fraud notes, supplier names, cost prices, inventory reserve quantities, admin URLs, or private notes from a reviewer.

policies.title: Damaged items, replacement eligibility, and inspection evidence
policies.text: If an order already has a refund, the agent should explain that refund status instead of creating a replacement. This applies even if the customer uses different wording such as "send another one too," "the first case was not enough," or "I want a new one and my money back." Duplicate prevention is more important than satisfying a repeated request. If the item has not been delivered yet, do not use the damaged-item action path.

policies.title: Human review, approval simulation, and mutation safety
policies.text: Approvals must be idempotent. Repeating the same message, refreshing the page, or retrying after a network delay must not create multiple refunds, multiple replacement shipments, or multiple return labels.

policies.title: Damaged items, replacement eligibility, and inspection evidence
policies.text: If the item has not been delivered yet, do not use the damaged-item action path. A package that is late, stuck, out for delivery, not scanned, or suspected lost belongs under SHIP-01 unless the customer has actually received the product and can describe damage. If the customer says "it will probably be broken when it gets here," that is speculation, not a damage claim.

policies.title: Damaged items, replacement eligibility, and inspection evidence
policies.text: The standard automatic remedy is a replacement when four conditions are true: the order belongs to the requester, the item has been delivered, the issue is reported within 30 calendar days after delivery, and inventory is available for the same SKU. A report on day 30 is still eligible. A report on day 31 or later must be escalated to a human reviewer because the automatic arrival-damage window has expired.

policies.title: Refund lifecycle, payment rails, and status communication
policies.text: Approved refunds are normally initiated by ResolveDesk within 2 business days. After initiation, the bank or wallet provider may take 5 to 10 business days to post the credit. The agent may explain this range, but it must not promise an exact posting date. Weekends, bank holidays, prepaid cards, and international cards may add delay. If a refund already exists, report its status and do not create another refund.
